findings.description: Data-model correctness: Page 03 claims the existing EmployeeSkill @@unique([employeeId, skillId]) IS the BR-18 single-record key, but it only enforces single-record per skillId. The BR-18 invariant requires one record per SEMANTIC skill. The verified starter schema has Skill.name @unique only (schema.prisma:42) and no canonicalKey; Page 03 adds canonicalKey but does NOT mark it unique nor define how resolveCanonicalSkill forces a semantic match to reuse one Skill.id. Two Skill rows for the same concept (e.g. 'TypeScript' vs 'TS') would allow two EmployeeSkill rows — the exact hero-loop duplicate-row failure signature P4/AC-22 exist to prevent.
findings.suggestion: Mark Skill.canonicalKey @unique (or have resolveCanonicalSkill upsert/return the canonical Skill.id by canonicalKey), and restate Page 03 §1/§6.1 as 'single-record per CANONICAL skill — @@unique is necessary but not sufficient until skillId is resolved to the canonical Skill.'

findings.description: Extra live-model dependency on the P0 hero write path: Page 02 §4.1 places the Claude skill-identity de-dupe call synchronously inside confirmCertExtraction (the loop's promote step), adding a second model call beyond the parse, with NO specified behavior if skill-identity fails or is unreachable. The parse path has an explicit failure UX; the identity call does not — so the most-protected loop step can hang/error after a successful parse+confirm.
findings.suggestion: Specify the skill-identity failure fallback on the write path (e.g. use a deterministic canonicalKey normalization as the persistence key with Claude only suggesting merges, or treat identity-call failure as create-as-new-and-reconcile) so a single P0 step does not depend on two live model calls. Composes with TS-001.

findings.description: API contract ambiguity: runMatch is listed in the Server Actions (mutations) table (Page 02 §3.1) yet annotated 'may be an action or a handler'. A staffing search is a read, not a mutation, and the transport is left undecided on a P0 capability — affecting caching and idempotency reasoning.
findings.suggestion: Decide and document runMatch transport (recommend an RSC data function or a read-only GET Route Handler), and move it out of the mutations table.

findings.description: Idempotency not DB-enforced: ADR-004 / Page 02 §3.2 / Page 03 §6.1 key idempotency on (employeeId, contentHash) and call it the integrity backbone of the loop, but the data model declares no DB uniqueness constraint on contentHash for Certificate/Resume. It relies on an app-layer 'seen before?' check only, which is racy under genuine double-submit (AC-23 / BR-19).
findings.suggestion: Add @@unique([employeeId, contentHash]) to Certificate and Resume in Page 03 so AC-23 idempotency is DB-enforced, matching the rigor applied to the BR-18 key.

council_flags.title: Auth.js (NextAuth) adoption for real Google OAuth (ADR-001)
council_flags.description: ADR-001 introduces Auth.js (NextAuth) + Google OIDC as a net-new third-party auth dependency not in the current-state stack (current-state records 'Auth: none, missing entirely'). Real authentication is a security-boundary + new-vendor/library decision. ADR-001 is well-reasoned (Clerk/Auth0/hand-rolled alternatives considered; PII-storing SaaS correctly rejected), so this is a SOFT flag for parallel council visibility, not a stop. The task explicitly named Auth.js as a council trigger to detect.
council_flags.rationale: Under NULogic council policy a new auth library + external IdP normally warrants council visibility. Cannot be independently cleared here because arch-council-policy.md is absent from this environment (see report §0). Anthropic SDK is NOT flagged — it is CLAUDE.md-mandated and already in the installed stack.

standards_availability_caveat: architecture-principles/*.md, adr-policy.md (T1-T23 ADR triggers), and arch-council-policy.md (C-triggers) were NOT found in this environment. Review proceeded against the effective in-repo baseline (CLAUDE.md non-negotiables, NULogic org instructions, current-state 03-tech-stack.md, and task-named council heuristics). YELLOWs therefore name the deviation + corrective action rather than citing an ADR-policy trigger number; the Auth.js council flag is raised for visibility and could not be definitively cleared. Recommend re-run with real standards files.
